dialogue.speaker: Rustam
dialogue.text: Okay, we need a few things. I've got the list. How much money have we got?

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: About 4,000 tenge. Not a lot, but enough for the basics.

dialogue.speaker: Rustam
dialogue.text: Perfect. We need some rice — how much should we get?

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: Get a kilo. That's enough for both of us for a week.

dialogue.speaker: Rustam
dialogue.text: Good. We don't have much oil left — I'll grab a small bottle.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: Don't get too much — we don't use a lot of oil. A 500ml bottle is plenty.

dialogue.speaker: Rustam
dialogue.text: Fine. How many eggs should I get?

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: A dozen should do it. We go through quite a few each week.

dialogue.speaker: Rustam
dialogue.text: Vegetables — I'm thinking carrots, onions, potatoes. How many bags?

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: Don't buy too many. One bag of each is enough. We don't have much space in the fridge.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: Get one loaf. We don't need much — I don't eat a lot of bread.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: We've got plenty of tea. But we're running low on coffee — get a small pack.

dialogue.speaker: Rustam
dialogue.text: Okay. I think we've got enough for everything. Shall we go through the totals?

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: Let's see — rice, oil, eggs, three bags of veg, bread, coffee. That should come to about 3,500. We'll have a little left.

questions.text: "How much oil should we get?" — Why "much" not "many"?
questions.hint: "much" is used with UNCOUNTABLE nouns (oil, rice, money, water). "many" is for COUNTABLE nouns (eggs, bags).

questions.text: "How many eggs should I get?" — Why "many" not "much"?
questions.hint: "many" is used with COUNTABLE nouns (one egg, two eggs...). "how many eggs?" ✅

questions.text: "We don't have ___ oil left." (not much — small amount)
questions.hint: "not much oil" — oil is uncountable → use "much". "We don't have much oil." ✅
"vegetables" = countable → "too MANY vegetables." "Too much" = uncountable food.

questions.text: "We've got plenty of tea." "Plenty of" means:
questions.hint: "plenty of" = more than enough; sufficient quantity. "Plenty of tea" = lots of tea, no need to buy more.
"a little" = a small amount (uncountable). "We'll have a little money left." ✅

questions.text: "We go through quite a few eggs." "Quite a few" means:
opts: a notable number (not a lot but significant)
questions.correct: a notable number (not a lot but significant)
questions.hint: "quite a few" = a noticeable number; more than just a little. "Quite a few eggs" = several eggs.

questions.text: "That's enough for both of us." — "Enough" expresses:
questions.hint: "enough" = sufficient; just the right amount. "Enough for both of us" = sufficient for two people.
